newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan antelope in peril through overhunting.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan antelope in peril through overhunting.

text.p: Kazakhstan's hunters are illegally slaughtering large numbers of saiga antelope and selling their antlers to China for use in traditional medicines, a local newspaper said on Wednesday.
The daily Karavan Blitz quoted environmental officials from the Aktyubinsk region, near the border with Russia, as saying they found 200 antlers stored at a remote hunting lodge.
The paper ran a banner headline over a picture of a wolf and a hunter declaring: "Worse than a wolf -- man."

Kazakh law says hunters can only shoot one percent of a saiga herd migrating across the semi-desert steppeland, but the report said these hunters had forged licences. The antlers are used in traditional medicine across the border in China.
Figures for the falling saiga population were not available but the antelope's meat, eaten regularly by the 16.9 million population a decade ago, is no longer found in shops.
The newspaper said lower numbers of saiga meant the region's large wolf packs were going hungry. "The wolves will soon be eating us," a regional official told the newspaper.
